investigations.name: sbml-decomposition
investigations.title: SBML in Tellurium vs process-bigraph decomposition — speed × accuracy × composability, and the limits of SBML itself
investigations.question: When you have a biochemical model, when should you run it monolithically in Tellurium (libroadrunner/CVODE) and when is it worth decomposing it into vivarium / process-bigraph sub-processes — and what does each point on that spectrum cost in performance and accuracy, buy in composability, and where does Tellurium (and SBML itself) stop being the right tool as models get larger or stop being reaction networks at all?
investigations.hypothesis: Across the spectrum monolithic Tellurium → operator-split → modular → fully-native process-bigraph, performance and accuracy degrade monotonically while composability rises, so no point dominates. Beyond the single-model comparison we predict two boundaries: (a) the monolithic libroadrunner build strains superlinearly as models scale, so decomposition's modularity matters at size even though it is not free on wall-clock; and (b) not every model is expressible as SBML — an agent-based model reduces to an SBML/ODE only in the large-population, well-mixed, deterministic limit.
